summary: A is meaningfully closer to the frozen contract because it keeps the change scoped to the new upload API and avoids altering global request/retry behavior. It still needs revision before merge, chiefly to delegate to FilesService.Add and add the contract-required tests.
reasons: Both implementations incorrectly duplicate FilesService.Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the multipart body through Add.
A reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile, validates both required inputs before body construction, propagates reader errors, and leaves Add and shared retry machinery unchanged.

B explicitly changes RawClient.Do to buffer nearly every non-native io.Reader across the SDK, directly violating the instruction not to refactor unrelated request/retry machinery and changing Files.Add, Files.Update, and other APIs’ memory and source-read timing semantics.

B’s changelog and README advertise the forbidden global behavior change, increasing the scope and compatibility surface that reviewers would need to unwind before merging materially more than A’s localized defect merits handling in this patch.
risks_a: Upload calls Raw.Do directly rather than FilesService.Add, creating duplicate machinery and risking future semantic drift.
Tests do not assert uploaded content, validation behavior, source-reader failure propagation, or an end-to-end Upload retry with streamed input.
The retry test only proves the already-known net/http replayability of bytes.Reader and is weakly connected to Upload.
risks_b: Global buffering of arbitrary io.Reader bodies is outside the frozen scope and can introduce large memory use, eager blocking, and changed error timing throughout the SDK.
Upload still bypasses FilesService.Add despite the explicit reuse requirement.
Although B’s Upload tests cover the requested cases substantially better, several RawClient and Files.Add tests verify behavior the contract specifically says not to introduce.
